findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the white and tinted backgrounds stop alternating after the tinted m3. m2, proof-1, proof-1-charts and proof-2 are four white sections in a row (proof-1-charts tints only its chart panel), from 'Samples, Order Confirmations…' down to the tinted 'Trial Runs'. The same shows on mobile.
findings.reference: The competitor tells neighbouring sections apart by their background.
findings.fix: Have the template's alternation treat proof-1, proof-1-charts and proof-2 (text sections that run on from one another) as one plain section and tint that group through --section-tint. The page then reads m3 (tint), m2 (white), proof group (tint), process-1, related and cta-steps alternating from there. Do not tint the sections one by one in reference.css.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: two iconList sections of the same shape stand one under the other. m3 and m2 each put a large heading and a lead on the left and a column of check-marked short items on the right, and only the background changes between them.
findings.reference: The competitor does not repeat a module back to back. This site's rule also says one of two same-shaped neighbours is laid out differently.
findings.fix: When two iconList sections are neighbours, have the template lay one of them out differently, for example m2's items as a two-column grid under its heading.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the heading 'Quality Claims, Returns and Outside Vendor Liability' breaks over four uneven lines and leaves 'Outside' alone on the third. m2's 'Samples, Order Confirmations, Shipping and Refunds' likewise leaves 'Shipping' alone on a line.
findings.reference: The competitor's headings break into even lines.
findings.fix: Add text-wrap: balance to the section h2 in the template's heading fit, so its lines break evenly without changing the fitted size.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the title 'From your brief to shipment: the typical order path' is still a lead, not the section's h2. It stands at about half the size of the other section headings on the page ('Trial Runs', 'Related products and services'), and the left column beside the six steps stays mostly empty. On mobile it also reads smaller than the section headings around it.
findings.reference: The competitor's step modules put a section heading over the steps, at the same level as its other section headings.
findings.fix: Have the template render the process list variant's title as the section h2, fitted like the other headings and starting on the content's left edge. The site's lead rule in reference.css (`.block--process .point-list__intro:not(:has(h2)) > .block__lead`) then no longer applies here.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: on phones the closing band crops its wide photo to a near-square frame centred on the woman. The heading 'Send Your Enquiry to Strandmill' and the lead sit right over her face and body. The darker overlay keeps the text readable but hides the subject, and changing object-position cannot clear her within this narrow window.
findings.reference: On desktop the same band puts its text on the empty dune to the left and leaves the subject clear on the right.
findings.fix: Give the cta band a different photo crop for narrow widths (art-direction), with the subject low or to one side, so the copy falls on an empty part of the photo.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the large heading 'Related products and services' sits over a single small link, 'Privacy Policy', which is neither a product nor a service. The same shows on mobile.
findings.reference: The competitor's onward links say where they lead (e.g. 'Read the full group story … at PT King Trading.').
findings.fix: In Site Factory, either link this page to the product or service pages about ordering, or retitle the block to fit its link (for example 'Related policies').
